statement: To find medial straight lines commensurable in square only which contain a rational rectangle.
heath_proof: Let two rational straight lines A, B commensurable in square only be set out; let C be taken a mean proportional between A, B, [VI. 13] and let it be contrived that, as A is to B, so is C to D. [VI. 12]  Then, since A, B are rational and commensurable in square only, the rectangle A, B, that is, the square on C [VI.17], is medial. [X. 21] Therefore C is medial. [X. 21] And since, as A is to B, so is C to D, and A, B are commensurable in square only, therefore C, D are also commensurable in square only. [X. 11] And C is medial; therefore D is also medial. [X. 23, addition] Therefore C, D are medial and commensurable in square only. I say that they also contain a rational rectangle. For since, as A is to B, so is C to D, therefore, alternately, as A is to C, so is B to D. [V. 16] But, as A is to C, so is C to B; therefore also, as C is to B, so is B to D; therefore the rectangle C, D is equal to the square on B. But the square on B is rational; therefore the rectangle C, D is also rational. Therefore medial straight lines commensurable in square only have been found which contain a rational rectangle.

**Statement:** To find medial straight lines commensurable in square only which contain a rational rectangle.

**Step 1.** Let A be the assigned rational straight line. By 10.10 find a straight line B incommensurable in length only with A, that is, such that the square on B is commensurable with the square on A while B is incommensurable in length with A. Then B is commensurable in square with A (D10.1.2), and since A is rational, B is rational also (D10.1.3). Thus A, B are two rational straight lines commensurable in square only.

**Step 2.** Between A and B take a mean proportional C (6.13), so that A : C = C : B.

**Step 3.** To the three straight lines A, B, C find a fourth proportional D (6.12), so that A : B = C : D.

**Step 4.** Since A : C = C : B, the three straight lines A, C, B are proportional; therefore the rectangle contained by the extremes A, B is equal to the square on the mean C (6.17).

**Step 5.** Since A, B are rational straight lines commensurable in square only, the rectangle A, B is irrational, and the side of the square equal to it is medial (10.21). But the square on C is equal to the rectangle A, B (Step 4); therefore C is medial (10.21).

**Step 6.** Since A : B = C : D, and A is incommensurable in length with B (Step 1), therefore C is incommensurable in length with D (10.11).

**Step 7.** Again, since the four straight lines A, B, C, D are proportional, the squares on them, being similar figures similarly described upon them, are also proportional: sq(A) : sq(B) = sq(C) : sq(D) (6.22). But the square on A is commensurable with the square on B, since A, B are commensurable in square (D10.1.2); therefore the square on C is commensurable with the square on D (10.11), that is, C and D are commensurable in square (D10.1.2).

**Step 8.** From Steps 6 and 7, C, D are commensurable in square only. And C is medial (Step 5), and D is commensurable with C (in square); therefore D is also medial (10.23). Therefore C, D are medial straight lines commensurable in square only.

**Step 9.** Since A : B = C : D, alternately A : C = B : D (5.16).

**Step 10.** But A : C = C : B (Step 2). Since the ratios C : B and B : D are each the same as the ratio A : C, therefore C : B = B : D (5.11).

**Step 11.** Hence C, B, D are three proportional straight lines, so the rectangle contained by the extremes C, D is equal to the square on the mean B (6.17).

**Step 12.** Now the square on A, the assigned rational straight line, is rational (D10.1.4), and the square on B is commensurable with it (Step 1); therefore the square on B is rational (D10.1.4). The rectangle C, D, being equal to the square on B (Step 11), is measured by the same measure as the square on B and is therefore commensurable with the square on A (D10.1.1); hence the rectangle C, D is rational (D10.1.4).

**Step 13.** Therefore C, D are medial straight lines commensurable in square only (Step 8) which contain a rational rectangle (Step 12); that is, medial straight lines commensurable in square only which contain a rational rectangle have been found. Q.E.F.
